pending_commit.commit_message: nebraska: Change Port() to GetPort() to be more descriptive BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittests Change-Id: If2ae52e35811e7908ce69e2ccb0c9ab482d8b3ce Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518800 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

nebraska: Add options to write port, pid, and log into specific files. - Add --runtime-root flag so users can specify a directory where we write these two files into: * port - To specify the port nebraska is serving, so a remote caller can use this port value to send request to nebraska. * pid - To specify the pid of the nebraska, so a remote caller can gracefully kill the nebraska using this pid value. - Add --log-file flag to specify a file for nebraska to write the logs into. If not passed it logs into stdout/stderr. We need to log to a specific file so after the update/install process was finished/failed, we can copy the log back and looking at it for debugging purposes. We should not log into syslog as it gets messed up with the other logs in the system and it makes it very hard to debug things. There are a lot of XML requests/responses that are generated by the nebraska and it is ideal for us to be able to look at the log all by itself and figure out what went wrong. BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittest TEST=cros flash with some custom code to run and kill nebraska succeeds. Change-Id: Id42afb4981467c73af90f3053988ba24b36aed84 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1496961 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

nebraska: Use signal handlers instead of waiting for input Use signals instead of input for properly exiting the server. The previous approach would fail when a remote SSH connection kills the nebraska. Users running locally can easily do CTRL + C to kill the process. BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unitests TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: I759a85b84d2525098e506a799cfb2a32c1c74745 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518801 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Xiaochu Liu <xiaochu@chromium.org>

nebraska: Change --{update|install}-payloads flags Change --update-payloads to --update-metadata to accurately describe what the directory is. We only look for the payload.json files in this directory and we don't care where the actual payloads are located. The payloads themselves are located/served by --payload-address. -- Same above change for install-payloads (-> install-metadata) BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittest TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: I074ca520938d0ad76ee45336cb243860e0e92344 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518802 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org>

nebraska: Break --payload-addr into two flags Currently, the nebraska adds /update or /install to the --payload-addr flag based on whether the request is install or update. But this is unfair to the server/service that serves the payload. They have to change their code semantics in order to handle this. Even more complicated we send an Omaha request to a devserver address like: "http://devserver-address/update" so the devserver so can send a response back. Now adding /update or /install to the end of addresses like this can become more confusing and cumbersome. So instead of nebraska making such assumptions, we should directly pass the addresses for install and updates to nebraska. If no address for install was passed we use the update address instead. So flag --payload-addr was replaced by two flags --update-payloads-address and --install-payloads-address. BUG=chromium:920404 TEST=unittest TEST=./nebraska.py Change-Id: Iaebc3e78a4d80f7085464c87b62622d7129ea66b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1518803 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

shill: Add exponential backoff to portal detection and remove portal check interval from profile Portal detection currently does the following (assuming that the user does not authenticate to the portal): send 3 probes spaced apart by 3 seconds. Each batch of 3 probes will be sent every 30 seconds until the portal is authenticated to. This change modifies it so that the second probe will be sent 3 seconds after the first one, the third probe 6 seconds after the second, and so on until a maximum interval of 300 seconds is reached. The retry values are tentative and subject to change. The initial portal check interval used to be configurable in the profile, but we no longer need this. Remove this as well. TODO: remove PortalAttempts histogram BUG=chromium:903645 TEST=1) unittests, 2) deployed shill to DUT and connected to portalled network. Retries exponentially backed off until 5 minutes. After authentication the retry interval is reset to 3.
